data.name: Iyappan
data.gender_notes: Iyappan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ayyappan is a name of Lord Ayyappan, a deity worshipped in Kerala and Tamil Nadu. He is believed to protect devotees from all dangers and fulfill their desires. His name is derived from the words ayyam (eternal) and pada (foot), indicating that he is the lord who is always present and protects with his feet. The name Iyappan carries the meaning “Lord Ayyappan” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Iyappan usually hope their child will grow to embody lord ayyappan and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of eternal protection and devotion
data.etymology: Iyappan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Ayyappan.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Iyappan total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Ayyappan is a significant cultural figure in the Indian subcontinent, especially in the states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. He is believed to be a composite form of Lord Shiva, Lord Vishnu, and Lord Ayyman, an ancient demon king. The deity's cultural importance can be seen through the numerous temples dedicated to him, the large number of pilgrims who travel to these temples annually, and the unique traditions and rituals associated with his worship.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, Lord Ayyappan is an embodiment of innocence, devotion, and purity. He is believed to protect his devotees from all dangers and adversities, and to grant them blessings and fulfill their desires. He is often invoked for healing, especially for those suffering from physical or emotional ailments. The spiritual significance of his name, derived from the words ayyam (eternal) and pada (foot), highlights his eternal presence and protection, symbolizing the belief that God is always with us, always present, and always ready to help.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Iyappan is a name revered in South India, symbolizing compassion, healing, and wisdom. It is believed that Iyappan, the lord of medicine, bestows health and prosperity upon his devotees.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Iyappan is mentioned in the Tamil epic Silappatikaram The name Iyappan carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
